ROOT <- normalizePath(getwd(), mustWork = TRUE)
DATA <- file.path(ROOT, "Publication", "datasets")
FIGURES <- file.path(ROOT, "Publication", "figures")
REPORT_SOURCE <- file.path(ROOT, "Publication", "Desmognathus_study_data.Rmd")

source(file.path(ROOT, "scripts", "publication", "gbe_theme.R"))
knitr::read_chunk(file.path(ROOT, "scripts", "publication", "build_gbe_figures.R"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

manifest <- read_csv(
  file.path(DATA, "DATASET_MANIFEST.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)

manifest_row <- function(supplement_id) {
  row <- manifest %>% filter(.data$supplement_id == .env$supplement_id)
  if (nrow(row) != 1L) stop("Expected one manifest row for ", supplement_id)
  row
}

read_supp <- function(supplement_id) {
  row <- manifest_row(supplement_id)
  read_csv(
    file.path(DATA, row$filename[[1]]),
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    progress = FALSE
  )
}

show_table <- function(data, rows = 10L, columns = 12L) {
  rmarkdown::paged_table(
    data,
    options = list(
      rows.print = min(rows, nrow(data)),
      cols.print = min(columns, ncol(data))
    )
  )
}

sha256_file <- function(path) {
  output <- system2("sha256sum", path, stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  if (length(output) != 1L) stop("Could not hash ", path)
  strsplit(output, "[[:space:]]+")[[1]][[1]]
}

species_label <- function(x) {
  text <- as.character(x)
  ifelse(grepl("^D\\. ", text), text, paste("D.", text))
}

figure_path <- function(filename) {
  path <- file.path(FIGURES, filename)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing figure: ", path, ". Run `make figures`.")
  path
}

stopifnot(
  nrow(manifest) == 40L,
  identical(manifest$supplement_id, sprintf("S%02d", seq_len(40)))
)

This is a read-only researcher-facing view over the controlled study release. The CSV files and their hashes remain the data authority. Code chunks make the filters and equations visible; the report does not overwrite a source table, review decision, or publication dataset.

Claim boundaries. Relative nuclear IOD is an image-derived relative phenotype, not an independently validated absolute genome size. The separate D. fuscus scale uses an assembly-derived conditional anchor of 16.462167689 pg/1C (16.1 Gbp / 0.978 Gbp per pg). The LTR terminal:internal statistic is a mapping/deletion-footprint proxy, not a direct ectopic-recombination, solo-LTR, or DNA-loss rate. Cell and nucleus summaries describe the reviewed upper tail of observed erythrocytes and their intervals are conditional on the observed animals and images. Current path analyses are exploratory and do not orient a unique causal arrow.

Study report

Guide and dataset index

What is included

  • TE34: 34 species with accession-linked genomic resources.
  • Path24: 24 species with finalized cell, nucleus, and relative-IOD data.
  • overlap21: the exact 21-species intersection; no TE or phenotype values are imputed.
  • S01–S40: controlled CSV supplements with source/output SHA-256 hashes.
  • Figures: the exact current ggplot figures built by scripts/publication/build_gbe_figures.R.

The report shows compact species-level tables directly. Large object- and element-level tables remain downloadable CSVs so the HTML stays responsive.

manifest %>%
  select(
    supplement_id,
    analysis_section,
    title,
    release_status,
    manuscript_use,
    rows,
    columns,
    filename,
    output_sha256
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 9)

Exact ggplot code and current figure

The following collapsed source chunk is the production ggplot code, read from the single figure builder rather than copied into this report.

# Figure 1: focal time tree, analysis design, genomic resources, and dnaPipeTE QC.
te_panel <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S02_te_resource_panel34.csv")
path_panel <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S03_path_analysis_panel24.csv")
path_traits <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S04_path_analysis_traits24.csv")
tree_audit_edges <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S38_phylogeny_edges.csv")
tree_audit_nodes <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S39_phylogeny_nodes.csv")
tree_path <- file.path(DATA, "trees", "desmognathus_time_tree_path24_v1.nwk")
path_tree <- ladderize(read.tree(tree_path), right = FALSE)

tip_count <- Ntip(path_tree)
node_count <- Nnode(path_tree)
root_distance <- node.depth.edgelength(path_tree)
root_age <- max(root_distance[seq_len(tip_count)])
node_age <- root_age - root_distance
node_y <- node.height(path_tree)

tree_horizontal <- tibble(
  parent = path_tree$edge[, 1],
  child = path_tree$edge[, 2]
) %>%
  mutate(
    x = node_age[parent],
    xend = node_age[child],
    y = node_y[child],
    yend = node_y[child]
  )
tree_vertical <- tibble(parent = sort(unique(path_tree$edge[, 1]))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    x = node_age[parent],
    ymin = min(node_y[path_tree$edge[path_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]]),
    ymax = max(node_y[path_tree$edge[path_tree$edge[, 1] == parent, 2]])
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
tree_tips <- tibble(
  node = seq_len(tip_count),
  tree_tip = path_tree$tip.label,
  x = 0,
  y = node_y[seq_len(tip_count)]
) %>%
  left_join(
    path_traits %>% select(species, tree_tip),
    by = "tree_tip",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

audit_tip_labels <- tree_audit_nodes %>%
  filter(is_tip) %>%
  pull(tip_label)
if (
  tip_count != 24L ||
    node_count != 23L ||
    nrow(tree_horizontal) != 46L ||
    nrow(tree_vertical) != 23L ||
    nrow(tree_audit_edges) != 46L ||
    nrow(tree_audit_nodes) != 47L ||
    any(is.na(tree_tips$species)) ||
    !setequal(path_tree$tip.label, path_traits$tree_tip) ||
    !setequal(path_tree$tip.label, audit_tip_labels) ||
    !isTRUE(all.equal(
      tree_horizontal$x - tree_horizontal$xend,
      path_tree$edge.length,
      tolerance = 1e-12,
      check.attributes = FALSE
    )) ||
    abs(root_age - max(tree_audit_nodes$root_distance_myr)) > 1e-4
) {
  stop("Figure 1 requires the exact audited 24-tip Path24 time tree")
}
if (
  !is.rooted(path_tree) ||
    !is.binary(path_tree) ||
    !is.ultrametric(path_tree, tol = 1e-6) ||
    any(path_tree$edge.length < 0)
) {
  stop("Figure 1 Path24 tree must be rooted, binary, time-scaled, and have nonnegative edges")
}

phylogeny_a <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(
    data = tree_horizontal,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
    linewidth = 0.35,
    lineend = "square",
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = tree_vertical,
    aes(x = x, xend = x, y = ymin, yend = ymax),
    linewidth = 0.35,
    lineend = "square",
    colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = tree_tips,

  )

panel_counts <- tibble(

  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 38), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +

design_b <- ggplot(assembly, aes(assembly_span_gb, contig_n50_kb)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.2, stroke = 0.35, fill = GBE_COLORS[["orange"]], colour = GBE_COLORS[["charcoal"]]) +
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(assembly, !is.na(label)), aes(label = label), size = GBE_LABEL_SIZE_MM, fontface = "italic", min.segment.length = 0, max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 20260713) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_number()) +

design_c <- ggplot(dnapipete_qc, aes(repeat_aligned_fraction_of_sample, order_unresolved_fraction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(dnapipete_qc$order_unresolved_fraction, na.rm = TRUE), linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.35, colour = GBE_COLORS[["gray"]]) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = n_dnapipete_runs > 1), size = 2.1, colour = GBE_COLORS[["green"]]) +

TE diversity and PCA

Diversity equations and primary filter

For proportions \(p_i\) within a species:

\[ H' = -\sum_i p_i \ln(p_i) \]

\[ D_{GS} = 1 - \sum_i p_i^2 \]

These are natural-log Shannon entropy and the Gini-Simpson index.

The paper-facing primary stratum is te_level == "order". Observed richness is retained only as an audit count, and the superfamily stratum is retained as a sensitivity/audit view. S08 contains classified-only diversity: classified categories are reclosed to one within each species. Unresolved aligned-base mass remains separate in S07 as dnaPipeTE classification-accounting QC and is not treated as a diversity category.

te_diversity <- read_supp("S08")
order_composition <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data",
    "te_order_composition.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

primary_diversity <- te_diversity %>%
  filter(te_level == "order")

recomputed_primary <- order_composition %>%
  pivot_longer(-species, names_to = "feature", values_to = "proportion") %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    observed_richness = sum(proportion > 0),
    shannon_entropy = -sum(proportion[proportion > 0] * log(proportion[proportion > 0])),
    gini_simpson = 1 - sum(proportion^2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_primary <- primary_diversity %>%
  select(species, observed_richness, shannon_entropy, gini_simpson) %>%
  arrange(species)

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_diversity) == 68L,
  nrow(primary_diversity) == 34L,
  n_distinct(te_diversity$species) == 34L,
  setequal(te_diversity$te_level, c("order", "superfamily")),
  nrow(te_diversity %>% count(te_level)) == 2L,
  all(te_diversity %>% count(te_level) %>% pull(n) == 34L),
  !any(grepl("unresolved", names(te_diversity), ignore.case = TRUE)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(recomputed_primary, observed_primary, tolerance = 1e-12))
)

primary_diversity %>%
  arrange(desc(shannon_entropy)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 5)

PCA normalization

The PCA uses retry-averaged superfamily compositions, retains features positive in all 34 TE species, closes each row, and applies the centered log-ratio transformation:

\[ \operatorname{clr}(p_{ij}) = \ln(p_{ij}) - \frac{1}{D}\sum_{k=1}^{D}\ln(p_{ik}) \]

Columns are centered and an unscaled SVD is fit. There is no zero replacement in the retained 24-superfamily matrix. CR1, Chapaev, Dada, Ginger, and Merlin remain available for diversity but fail the ubiquitous-feature PCA gate.

te_scores <- read_supp("S09")
te_variance <- read_supp("S10")
te_loadings <- read_supp("S11")
feature_prevalence <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data",
    "te_feature_prevalence.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

retained_superfamilies <- feature_prevalence %>%
  filter(te_level == "superfamily", pca_included)
excluded_superfamilies <- feature_prevalence %>%
  filter(te_level == "superfamily", !pca_included)

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_scores) == 34L,
  nrow(te_variance) == 23L,
  nrow(te_loadings) == 24L,
  nrow(retained_superfamilies) == 24L,
  setequal(
    excluded_superfamilies$feature,
    c("CR1", "Chapaev", "Dada", "Ginger", "Merlin")
  )
)

excluded_superfamilies %>%
  select(
    feature, n_species_positive, prevalence_fraction,
    minimum_proportion, maximum_proportion, pca_exclusion_reason
  )

No final sensitivity analysis asks whether forcing CR1 or Chapaev into the shared-feature PCA changes support; the report does not invent one.

Exact ggplot code and current figure

# Figure 2: TE diversity and compositional ordination.
te_diversity <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S08_te_diversity.csv") %>%
  filter(te_level == "order") %>%
  select(
    species,
    shannon_entropy,
    gini_simpson
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(shannon_entropy, gini_simpson),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "diversity_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = factor(
      recode(
        metric,
        shannon_entropy = "Shannon entropy",
        gini_simpson = "Gini-Simpson index"
      ),
      levels = c("Shannon entropy", "Gini-Simpson index")
    )
  )
diversity_counts <- te_diversity %>% count(metric)
if (
  n_distinct(te_diversity$species) != 34L ||
    nrow(diversity_counts) != 2L ||
    !all(diversity_counts$n == 34L)
) {
  stop("Figure 2 classified-only order diversity panel requires 34 species per metric")
}
te_scores <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S09_te_pca_scores.csv") %>%
  filter(te_level == "superfamily", composition_mode == "classified_conditional") %>%
  mutate(
    species_label = species_label(species),
    distance = sqrt(PC1^2 + PC2^2),
    label = if_else(rank(-distance, ties.method = "first") <= 10, species_label, NA_character_)
  )
te_variance <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S10_te_pca_variance.csv") %>%
  filter(PC <= 10)
pc1_variance <- te_variance %>% filter(PC == 1) %>% pull(variance_explained)
pc2_variance <- te_variance %>% filter(PC == 2) %>% pull(variance_explained)
if (length(pc1_variance) != 1L || length(pc2_variance) != 1L) {
  stop("Figure 2 requires one variance row for each of the first two PCs")
}

te_a <- ggplot(te_diversity, aes(x = "", y = diversity_value)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.55,

    fill = GBE_COLORS[["blue"]],

    shape = 21,
    size = 0.9,
    stroke = 0.2,
    fill = GBE_COLORS[["blue"]],
    colour = "white",
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(metric), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Order-level diversity") +
  theme_gbe() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),

  )

te_b <- ggplot(te_scores, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = GBE_COLORS[["light_gray"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = GBE_COLORS[["light_gray"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, colour = GBE_COLORS[["purple"]]) +
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(te_scores, !is.na(label)), aes(label = label), size = GBE_LABEL_SIZE_MM, fontface = "italic", max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0, seed = 20260713) +

Repeat landscape

The production plot selects the six reported categories with the greatest total aligned bases, combines the remainder as Other, zero-fills every species/category/divergence-bin combination, and gives all 34 species equal weight in the across-species curves. The young-repeat summary uses bins below 5% divergence.

repeat_landscape <- read_supp("S12")
repeat_inventory <- read_supp("S13")

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(repeat_landscape$species) == 34L,
  nrow(repeat_inventory) == 34L
)

repeat_inventory %>%
  arrange(desc(aligned_hit_bp)) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 4)

The full 13,371-row landscape is available as S12 CSV.

# Figure 3: RepeatMasker divergence landscape.
landscape <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S12_repeatmasker_divergence_landscape.csv")
top_categories <- landscape %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  summarise(hit_bp = sum(hit_bp), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(hit_bp, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  pull(order)
category_levels <- c(top_categories, "Other")
landscape_by_species <- landscape %>%
  mutate(repeat_category = if_else(order %in% top_categories, order, "Other")) %>%
  group_by(species, repeat_category, divergence_bin_start_pct) %>%
  summarise(percent_species_hit_bp = sum(percent_species_hit_bp), .groups = "drop") %>%
  right_join(
    expand_grid(
      species = sort(unique(landscape$species)),
      repeat_category = category_levels,
      divergence_bin_start_pct = 0:50
    ),
    by = c("species", "repeat_category", "divergence_bin_start_pct")
  ) %>%
  mutate(percent_species_hit_bp = replace_na(percent_species_hit_bp, 0))
if (
  n_distinct(landscape_by_species$species) != 34L ||
    nrow(landscape_by_species) != 34L * length(category_levels) * 51L
) {
  stop("Figure 3 landscape grid must zero-fill every TE34 category/bin combination")

LTR terminal:internal depth proxy

Gate and IQR replay

An eligible element is at least 3,000 bp long, has an exact TEsorter annotation, is LTR/Gypsy, and has at least five whitespace-delimited DOMAIN|MODEL annotations. The essential filter is inclusive and is computed within species over the 408 eligible elements:

\[ Q1 - 1.5\,IQR \leq T:I \leq Q3 + 1.5\,IQR \]

The independent coverage gate requires positive depth across at least 80% of positions separately in the left LTR, right LTR, and internal region. The primary branch is the intersection of IQR retention and that coverage gate.

ltr_elements <- read_supp("S14")
ltr_species <- read_supp("S15")
ltr_coverage <- read_supp("S16")
ltr_excluded <- read_supp("S17")

count_tesorter_domains <- function(value) {
  text <- trimws(as.character(value))
  if (is.na(value) || text == "" || tolower(text) == "none") return(0L)
  length(strsplit(text, "[[:space:]]+")[[1]])
}

ltr_check <- ltr_elements %>%
  mutate(
    recomputed_domain_count = vapply(Domains, count_tesorter_domains, integer(1)),
    recomputed_domain_gate =
      .data[["element length"]] >= 3000 &
      tesorter_annotation_found &
      Order == "LTR" &
      Superfamily == "Gypsy" &
      recomputed_domain_count >= 5
  )

fences <- ltr_check %>%
  filter(recomputed_domain_gate) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    q1 = quantile(ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions, 0.25),
    q3 = quantile(ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions, 0.75),
    iqr = q3 - q1,
    lower = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    upper = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ltr_check <- ltr_check %>%
  left_join(fences, by = "species") %>%
  mutate(
    recomputed_iqr_keep = recomputed_domain_gate &
      ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions >= lower &
      ratio_terminal_internal_all_positions <= upper,
    recomputed_coverage =
      left_ltr_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8 &
      right_ltr_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8 &
      internal_positive_coverage_fraction >= 0.8,
    recomputed_primary = recomputed_iqr_keep & recomputed_coverage
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(ltr_elements) == 1086L,
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_count == as.integer(ltr_check$domain_count)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate == as.logical(ltr_check$domain_gate_keep)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_iqr_keep == as.logical(ltr_check$iqr_filter_keep)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_coverage == as.logical(ltr_check$coverage_ge_80pct)),
  all(ltr_check$recomputed_primary == as.logical(ltr_check$primary_ltr_element)),
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate) == 408L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_iqr_keep) == 381L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_domain_gate & ltr_check$recomputed_coverage) == 407L,
  sum(ltr_check$recomputed_primary) == 380L,
  n_distinct(ltr_check$species[ltr_check$recomputed_primary]) == 30L
)

primary_ltr_species <- ltr_species %>%
  filter(
    analysis_branch == "primary_iqr_filtered_coverage_ge_80pct",
    ratio_median > 0
  ) %>%
  select(
    species, n_elements, ratio_median,
    median_bootstrap_ci_low, median_bootstrap_ci_high,
    fraction_ratio_gt_1,
    median_terminal_positive_coverage_fraction,
    median_internal_positive_coverage_fraction
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ratio_median))

stopifnot(nrow(primary_ltr_species) == 30L)
primary_ltr_species %>% show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)

The 1,086-row audit table remains intact; filtering changes branch membership instead of deleting evidence. No canonical between-species omnibus test has been finalized for this corrected 380-element branch, so none is added here.

The object table contains 1,152 frozen reviewed cell-nucleus pairs across 24 species; the report does not silently refilter it. Physical area uses the fixed conversion \(0.0144\;\mu m^2\) per pixel. Species point estimates are medians of the accepted reviewed pairs.

Relative nuclear IOD

Optical density is defined per nuclear-mask pixel from background and observed intensity; nuclear IOD is the sum of optical density over the mask, not mean optical density. The primary species estimator is the arithmetic mean of the within-image median IOD values. Dividing the 24 species estimates and their interval bounds by the Path24 median anchor produces the relative index:

\[ IOD_{relative,s} = \frac{\operatorname{mean}_{image} (\operatorname{median}_{nucleus}(IOD))_s} {\operatorname{median}_{species}(IOD_{equal-image})} \]

A separate descriptive scale uses the published rounded pooled D. fuscus assembly estimate. The declared conversion is:

\[ G_{reference,1C} = \frac{16.1\ \mathrm{Gbp}} {0.978\ \mathrm{Gbp\ pg}^{-1}} = 16.462167689\ \mathrm{pg} \]

Process_413/specimen 32469 and Process_414/specimen 32470 were author-confirmed as the D. fuscus standards and were stained in the same experimental runs as the unknowns. Their exact standard-to-target run map has not been recovered, and their median IOD values differ by approximately 41%. The picogram fields are therefore an assembly-derived conditional sensitivity scale, not an independently validated absolute C-value; relative_iod_index remains the primary phenotype.

iod_species <- read_supp("S22")

iod_balance <- read_supp("S24")

iod_anchor <- median(recomputed_iod$iod_equal_image_estimate)
recomputed_iod <- recomputed_iod %>%
  mutate(relative_iod_index = iod_equal_image_estimate / iod_anchor) %>%
  arrange(species)

observed_iod <- iod_species %>%

pgls <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S26_pairwise_pgls_sensitivity.csv")

pgls_panel <- function(data, comparison_id, x, y, x_low, x_high, y_low, y_high, x_label, y_label, colour, shape_variable = NULL) {
  stat <- pgls %>% filter(.data$comparison == .env$comparison_id) %>% slice(1)
  x_values <- data[[x]]
  y_values <- data[[y]]
  x_log <- log10(x_values)
  y_log <- log10(y_values)
  x_sequence <- seq(min(x_values), max(x_values), length.out = 200)
  x_z <- (log10(x_sequence) - mean(x_log)) / sd(x_log)
  predicted_z <- stat$pgls_intercept_z + stat$pgls_standardized_beta * x_z
  model_variance <- stat$pgls_var_intercept + 2 * x_z * stat$pgls_cov_intercept_slope + x_z^2 * stat$pgls_var_slope
  critical <- qt(0.975, stat$pgls_degrees_freedom)
  model <- tibble(
    x = x_sequence,
    fit = 10^(mean(y_log) + sd(y_log) * predicted_z),
    low = 10^(mean(y_log) + sd(y_log) * (predicted_z - critical * sqrt(pmax(model_variance, 0)))),
    high = 10^(mean(y_log) + sd(y_log) * (predicted_z + critical * sqrt(pmax(model_variance, 0))))
  )
  lambda_text <- ifelse(stat$pagel_lambda < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.2f", stat$pagel_lambda))
  p_text <- ifelse(
    stat$pgls_p_value < 0.001,
    "<0.001",
    paste("=", sprintf("%.3f", stat$pgls_p_value))
  )
  annotation <- sprintf(
    "PGLS beta = %.2f (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f)\nP %s; lambda %s; n = %d",
    stat$pgls_standardized_beta, stat$pgls_ci_low, stat$pgls_ci_high,
    p_text, lambda_text, stat$n_species
  )
  panel <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = .data[[y]])) +
    geom_ribbon(data = model, aes(x = x, ymin = low, ymax = high), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = colour, alpha = 0.12) +
    geom_line(data = model, aes(x = x, y = fit), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = colour, linewidth = 0.65) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = .data[[y_low]], ymax = .data[[y_high]]), width = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = alpha(colour, 0.35)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = .data[[x_low]], xmax = .data[[x_high]]), orientation = "y", width = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = alpha(colour, 0.35))
  if (is.null(shape_variable)) {
    panel <- panel + geom_point(shape = 21, size = 1.8, stroke = 0.3, fill = colour, colour = "white")
  } else {
    panel <- panel +
      geom_point(aes(shape = .data[[shape_variable]]), size = 2, stroke = 0.3, fill = colour, colour = "white") +
      scale_shape_manual(
        name = "IOD support",
        values = c(
          "Balanced multiple-image support" = 21,
          "One image and animal" = 24,
          "Quality-balance caution" = 23
        )
      )
  }
  panel +
    annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = annotation, hjust = -0.02, vjust = 1.3, size = GBE_LABEL_SIZE_MM) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = y_label) +
    theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5)
}

iod_a <- pgls_panel(
  pair_data, "relative_iod_vs_nucleus_area", "relative_iod_index", "nucleus_area_um2",
  "relative_iod_ci_low", "relative_iod_ci_high", "nucleus_area_um2_ci_low", "nucleus_area_um2_ci_high",
  "Relative nuclear IOD index", expression("Nucleus area ("*mu*"m"^2*")"), GBE_COLORS[["blue"]], "iod_support"
)
iod_b <- pgls_panel(
  pair_data, "relative_iod_vs_cell_area", "relative_iod_index", "cell_area_um2",
  "relative_iod_ci_low", "relative_iod_ci_high", "cell_area_um2_ci_low", "cell_area_um2_ci_high",
  "Relative nuclear IOD index", expression("Cell area ("*mu*"m"^2*")"), GBE_COLORS[["orange"]], "iod_support"
) + guides(shape = "none")
iod_c <- pgls_panel(
  morphology, "nucleus_area_vs_cell_area", "nucleus_area_um2", "cell_area_um2",
  "nucleus_area_um2_ci_low", "nucleus_area_um2_ci_high", "cell_area_um2_ci_low", "cell_area_um2_ci_high",
  expression("Nucleus area ("*mu*"m"^2*")"), expression("Cell area ("*mu*"m"^2*")"), GBE_COLORS[["purple"]]
)

Figure_6 <- iod_a + iod_b + iod_c +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 1), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", tag_prefix = "(", tag_suffix = ")") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")

record_figure(
  "Figure_6", "Figure_6_relative_iod_pairwise_pgls", 185, 92,
  "S19;S22;S24;S26",
  "Relative nuclear IOD, nucleus area, and cell area are positively associated in Pagel-lambda PGLS sensitivity fits. Circles identify balanced multiple-image IOD support, triangles identify balanced estimates from one image and animal, and diamonds identify four species that fail the declared quality-balance gate. Bars are conditional measurement-bootstrap intervals; lines and ribbons are PGLS fits and model confidence intervals. The IOD index is not an independently calibrated absolute genome size.",
  "Three scatterplots show relative nuclear IOD versus nucleus area, relative nuclear IOD versus cell area, and nucleus area versus cell area, each with measurement intervals and a phylogenetically corrected fitted line; point shape exposes single-image and quality-balance limitations in the IOD panels.",

)

Figure 6. Relative IOD, nucleus area, and cell area sensitivities.

Integrated species views

S40 is the exact 21-species TE34-by-Path24 overlap. The join is at species level; genomic and microscopy measurements are not from the same animal.

te_iod_overlap <- read_supp("S40")
organismal_traits <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    ROOT, "analyses", "03_phylogenetic_path", "data",
    "organismal_traits.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(te_iod_overlap) == 21L,
  n_distinct(te_iod_overlap$species) == 21L,
  nrow(organismal_traits) == 37L,
  n_distinct(organismal_traits$species) == 37L
)

te_iod_overlap %>%
  select(
    species, scientific_name, shannon_entropy, gini_simpson,
    relative_iod_index, relative_iod_ci_low, relative_iod_ci_high,
    manual_review_inclusion
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)

The expert reproductive-strategy categories are retained as vetted organismal traits, but the interpretation was supplied after review of the initial PCA. Any overlay is therefore post hoc and descriptive, not a confirmatory test.

organismal_traits %>%

    reproductive_strategy_source_id, organismal_source_ids

  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)

Existing frozen statistical sensitivities

This tab exposes existing frozen exploratory outputs so collaborators can inspect them. It does not promote them to confirmatory manuscript claims. The report does not run the previously discussed ad hoc power, omnibus, or univariate phylogenetic-signal calculations. No final between-species LTR test or diversity-index group test is added here.

The Path24 traits are log10-transformed and sample-standardized for the current three-trait analysis. Pairwise PGLS estimates Pagel’s lambda by maximum likelihood. The implemented model contains relative IOD, nucleus area, and cell area only; the possible integrated TE/SVL path model has not been specified or fitted.

pairwise_pgls <- read_supp("S26")
path_models <- read_supp("S30")
path_stability <- read_supp("S32")
path_simulation <- read_supp("S36")
path_dsep <- read_supp("S37")

pairwise_pgls %>%
  select(
    comparison, spearman_rho, p_value_descriptive_only,
    pearson_r, pearson_p_value_descriptive_only,
    pgls_standardized_beta, pgls_ci_low, pgls_ci_high,
    pgls_p_value, pagel_lambda, n_species
  ) %>%
  show_table(rows = 3, columns = 11)
path_models %>%
  filter(analysis_type == "primary") %>%
  arrange(delta_CICc) %>%
  show_table(rows = 10, columns = 12)

The complete frozen outputs S26–S37 are linked in the Downloads tab. Their code authority is analyses/03_phylogenetic_path/run_path_analysis.R.

The formal TE-PCA audit remains separate from the descriptive S08–S11 tables:

te_audit_dir <- file.path(ROOT, "analyses", "01_transposable_elements", "data")
te_cluster_diagnostics <- read_csv(
  file.path(te_audit_dir, "te_pca_clustering_diagnostics.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
te_cluster_stability <- read_csv(
  file.path(te_audit_dir, "te_pca_clustering_stability.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
te_trait_tests <- read_csv(
  file.path(te_audit_dir, "te_pca_trait_association_tests.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
te_phylogenetic_tests <- read_csv(
  file.path(te_audit_dir, "te_pca_phylogenetic_signal_tests.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

te_cluster_diagnostics %>%
  select(any_of(c(
    "candidate_id", "representation", "k", "cluster_sizes",
    "mean_silhouette", "gap_primary_selected_k", "accepted"
  ))) %>%
  show_table(rows = 12, columns = 8)
te_phylogenetic_tests %>% show_table(rows = 6, columns = 10)

No discrete PCA cluster is accepted. Tree-based results remain provisional until the collaborator tree’s publication/calibration provenance is supplied. The exact replay command is make te-pca; it is intentionally not rerun while knitting this report.

# Figure 7: exploratory relative-IOD path comparison and calibration.
path_models <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S30_path_model_comparison.csv") %>%
  filter(analysis_type == "primary") %>%
  arrange(delta_CICc) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(
    model_label = gsub("_", " ", model),
    model_label = sub("^iod", "IOD", model_label),
    model_label = factor(model_label, levels = rev(model_label))
  )
simulation <- read_supp("Supplementary_Data_S36_path_simulation_calibration.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    generating_label = gsub("_", " ", generating_class),
    generating_label = sub("^iod", "IOD", generating_label),
    residual_label = recode(residual_regime, iid = "Independent residuals", brownian = "Brownian residuals")
  )

path_a <- ggplot(
  path_models,
  aes(
    delta_CICc,
    model_label,
    colour = globally_supported,
    shape = globally_supported
  )
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.35, colour = GBE_COLORS[["gray"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 1.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = GBE_COLORS[["blue"]], `FALSE` = GBE_COLORS[["vermillion"]]), name = "Global fit", labels = c("Rejected", "Passed")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 17), name = "Global fit", labels = c("Rejected", "Passed")) +
  labs(x = expression(Delta*"CICc from best Path24 model"), y = NULL) +
  theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5)

path_b <- ggplot(
  simulation,
  aes(
    generating_label,
    true_class_top_rate,
    colour = residual_label,
    shape = residual_label,
    group = residual_label
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 1.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.45)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(GBE_COLORS[c("blue", "orange")]), name = "Simulation regime") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), name = "Simulation regime") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Generating equivalence class", y = "True-class top-model rate") +
  theme_gbe(base_size = 7.5) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 28, hjust = 1))

Figure_7 <- path_a + path_b +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.45, 1), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", tag_prefix = "(", tag_suffix = ")") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")

record_figure(
  "Figure_7", "Figure_7_exploratory_phylogenetic_path_sensitivity", 185, 108,
  "S30-S36",
  "The finalized 24-species relative-IOD path-model ranking favors one Markov-equivalence class, while simulation recovery varies by generating class and residual regime. Delta CICc is relative to the best Path24 model; color and shape record the global d-separation fit gate. The IOD node is standardized log10 relative nuclear IOD, not absolute genome size, and these results do not orient causal arrows within an equivalence class.",
  "The left panel compares candidate relative-IOD equivalence classes in the finalized 24-species analysis by delta CICc and global-fit status. The right panel shows true-class recovery rates under independent and Brownian residual simulations.",
  "sensitivity_only_relative_iod_no_causal_claim"
)

Figure 7. Exploratory Path24 model and simulation sensitivities.

Auxiliary DAG reference (unnumbered): the current Path24 analysis scores 10 testable Markov-equivalence classes and the auxiliary image below shows one representative DAG for each class. The saturated 6-member class is omitted because it has no d-separation claim and was not scored. Relative nuclear IOD is an image-derived relative phenotype, not absolute genome size, and the arrows shown here are representative only, not uniquely oriented causal claims.
